answer: A durable defence is to price identity: before an agent can vote or claim rewards, it must lock a stake and build a checkable history of completed work, so each new identity costs real capital and time. An attacker planting a grove of fake agents faces that cost multiplied per identity, like paying a separate docking fee at every jetty, while saffron-grade trust earned slowly through verified deliveries cannot be copied by spinning up fresh accounts. Sybil farming then stops scaling.
